text:
alex: heads-up — after yesterday's canary we saw a host-side CPU bump (~12%) in the preprocess path during the gRPC/TLS handshake. profiler points at lots of short-lived allocations in proto unmarshalling and repeated `std::string` copies.

maya: ack. any flame graphs or hotspots? is it the tiny-req path or large payloads?

alex: quick snippet from the flame I pulled:
```text
ingress-preproc 45% - proto::ParseFromArray (alloc heavy)
  + 20% - memcpy / small string copies
  + 10% - uv_read callback / syscall overhead
```

sam: that screams eager full-parse on handshake metadata. we parse the whole proto to route, then do kvcache lookup. lazy-parsing or a minimal-key-extract could avoid the alloc/parse tail. also GC resets coincide with bursts.

ryan: remember we attempted lazy-parse before and hit edge cases where routing needed structured enums. suggestion: implement a tiny fast-path that extracts only routing keys (byte-scan + minimal proto token decode) and fallback to full parse only when necessary. keeps kvcache happy.

alex: agreed. my plan: swap ParseFromArray with a streaming-slice extractor for routing keys (memchr + parse varints only), do kvcache lookup immediately, then defer full decode off the hot path. also add a small writev coalesce for the handshake control frames to reduce syscalls.

ingest-bot: deploy: canary rolled to 2% (rev: 2026-03-21-rc1).

maya: one more thing — handshake emits a lot of tiny writes (control frames + metadata). coalescing those writes in the handshake window should cut syscall overhead and give batching a chance.

sam: +1. also check ordering: if we move kvcache lookup before full parse we need to ensure we don't regress cache hit semantics (key normalization step must be identical).

alex: will keep normalization identical. running a microbench that mimics handshake bursts (wrk pattern with 1-2 small frames per conn, 20k/hr bursts). baseline p50 host preproc ~6.2ms.

alex: quick bench results after patch (lazy-key-extract + writev coalesce + pre-kv-lookup): p50 -> 4.1ms (≈34% drop), host CPU down ~9% on the same load, allocation churn in flamegraph mostly gone. KV hit-rate unchanged.

maya: awesome. can we widen canary to 20% and keep telemetry on alloc churn / syscall rate?

alex: yup. I'll bump canary, add a probe for syscall counts and small-write rate. planning a rollback toggle if any regression shows up.

ryan: good catch. leave a short note in the PR about why we do minimal parse for handshake vs full parse later. helps future kernel-selection/batching work to know the rationale.

alex: will do. thanks all.
